text:
Alice Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock the Q2 pricing matrix and add-on levers. AcmeCorp pushed back: they want a dedicated pool, higher token ceilings, and a contractual SLA. Need a decision this week so GTM can bake collateral.

Raj Patel: timeline noted. biggest risk is margin if we give higher caps without commitment. can we push them to a 12mo commit with ramping tiers? :thinking_face: 

Simone Lopez: Agreed. Propose two negotiation levers: (1) committed spend (discount tiers) (2) optional add-ons priced as flat monthly seat/pool fees. We should avoid open-ended per-token discounts.

Ben Walker: From infra POV, dedicated pools are straightforward if committed GPU hours are included. Operational cost ~= $X/hr per pool. We need a minimum commit to justify reserved nodes.

Raj Patel: if we set minimum at $50k/mo commit for dedicated pool, is that defensible? Sales needs a lower-footprint option for mid-market.

Simone Lopez: $50k/mo is the break-even ballpark. For mid-market, offer a Pro+ add-on: shared priority capacity with higher soft limits but no dedicated nodes. That can be $5k/mo + per-token.

Maya Singh: Legal note — any SLA tied to latency or uptime must include carve-outs for force majeure and cross-region outages. Also need clear definitions for "availability" and "inference latency" measurement points.

Tom Yates: Customer success wants a migration path: if a customer starts on Pro and later needs dedicated, we should offer a credits-based transition (port credit = 50% of unused prepay?). prevents churn during upgrades.

Alice Chen: This is useful. Draft launch criteria I'm thinking: (a) public price page for Core/Pro/Enterprise + documented add-ons, (b) internal pricing playbook with negotiation guardrails, (c) legal SLA templates, (d) mapping of support tiers. Can we commit to that by EOD Fri?

Ben Walker: EOD Fri is tight but doable if add-ons are parameterized. I'll provide resource cost estimates by Thu AM.

Simone Lopez: I'll run margin scenarios once Ben gives numbers. Quick ask: should per-embedding charges be separate? there's push from bench to unify token billing.

Raj Patel: Keep embeddings separate for now — enterprise buyers treat them differently and it's a negotiation lever. 

Alice Chen: OK keep embeddings an add-on line item. For the public matrix, high level only: Core (free tier limits), Pro ($2k/mo, 50M tokens incl), Pro+ (shared priority, $5k/mo), Enterprise (custom commit + dedicated pool). Add-ons: Dedicated Pool, Premium SLA, Advanced Retention, Embedding Pack.

billing-bot: Notice: proposed Pro list price $2000/mo will route to product-pricing for review.

Maya Singh: I'll prepare two SLA templates: "Standard" (response SLAs, best-effort latency) and "Premium" (penalized SLOs + credits). Need to confirm credit calculus with finance.

Tom Yates: Customer adoption check — recommend field playbook: thresholds to upsell = consistent 7d avg tokens > 40M or sustained p50 latency > 350ms.

Alice Chen: Final ask: Raj, can you get AcmeCorp to confirm commitment horizon? If they want <12mo, we'll offer Pro+/shared priority but not dedicated. If >=12mo commit, open Enterprise + dedicated pricing.

Raj Patel: will do. pinging @AcmeCorp contact after this thread.

Alice Chen: Great. Next steps -> Ben + Simone for numbers, Maya on SLA drafts, Raj on customer confirmation, Tom for playbook. Align Thu end-of-day for updated doc and Fri sign-off. :rocket:
